name: Noyau
purpose: Visual identity for Noyau, a French nonprofit correcting the public belief that nuclear power causes cancer. Every page reads from styles.css; swap the tokens below and the whole book re-renders.

brand.name: Noyau
brand.meaning: The nucleus of an atom · the stone at the centre of a fruit · the core or heart, as in le noyau familial, the family unit
brand.argument: The same word names the feared physics and the human warmth. The science people fear is the science that treats their children.
brand.trademark: NOT CLEARED. Searched only. A trademark attorney is required before registration or print.

personality.summary: The brand does not argue. It disarms.
personality.emotionalCentre: There is something good here — not you are safe. Hope is an offer; safety is a defensive claim.

color.note: Four codes per swatch. PMS values are UNVERIFIED starting points — Pantone cannot be matched on a screen. Match from a physical guide under D50 before ordering ink.
color.derivation: The brief demanded warmth and both obvious warm colours were occupied — amber by Réseau Sortir du Nucléaire, saturated yellow #FFE600 by Orano. A noyau is the stone of a stone fruit, and the fruit supplied a hue nobody in either category holds.

forbidden.reason: Fails outright. Light text on apricot is illegible. Use Terracotta for anything carrying light text.
They converge under colour blindness. Never encode meaning across that pair.

color.excludedHues: No blue anywhere. Six of seven childhood-cancer charities lead with blue; so do four of five pro-nuclear bodies. It is the most crowded hue in both categories.

display.note: A serif in a category that is uniformly sans. SOFT and WONK carry the informality — not a decorative script, which five of seven charities already use.

body.stack: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", "Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
body.note: Drawn by the Braille Institute for low vision. Derived from the ward legibility floor — this material is read by unwell children, tired parents and clinical staff.

type.fallbackRule: Fallbacks are the specification, not a footnote. For a volunteer typing a flyer on a ward computer, the fallback is what actually renders.
type.subsets: Both families carry latin-ext — verified. Covers Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian and Nordic diacritics for the Europe plan.

logo.description: A cooling tower with a wheat wreath, blossoming where the plume would be.
logo.clearSpaceUnit: X = the height of the tower, base excluded
logo.reducedVariant: Below ~32px use noyau-mark-small.svg — wheat and the two smaller blossoms are dropped, because at 16px they turn to grey fuzz.
logo.singleColour: The whole mark inherits one `color` attribute. All separations are real negative space, so it works reversed, on colour, on photographs, and in one-colour print, foil, engraving and embroidery.

pattern.name: Le Grain
meanings: the surface texture of a material — le grain du papier
the wheat standing in the mark
pattern.source: Route A — the brand's own material. A noyau is a fruit stone; its surface is grooved and pitted.
pattern.construction: Seamless 400×400 tile. 150 marks, toroidal Poisson sampling, angles from a flow field so the grain runs rather than scatters. 16% round pits.

openItems: PMS values are unverified starting points. Match from a physical guide under D50 lighting.
The public claim needs narrowing: normal operation of nuclear power does not measurably raise cancer risk, while high-dose radiation is carcinogenic — which is why it treats tumours.
Brand photography does not exist yet and must be commissioned. No free-licence library contains a volunteer sitting with a child in treatment.
